topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, learning outcomes, and the central question of what causes cancer.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Intrinsic Factors, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the nature of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and examine the interplay between intrinsic biological processes, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how bacterial, parasitic, and viral infections drive cancer development, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific chemical compounds, metabolic activation pathways, and UV radiation induce DNA adducts and mutational changes.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion and Non-Mutagenic Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate cancer initiators from promoters, explaining how non-mutagenic exposures drive tumorigenesis through chronic inflammation and intracellular signalling activation.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility and Principles of Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how tissue developmental stage, host age, and reproductive history modulate susceptibility to carcinogens before summarizing the core mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic mutational signatures, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo animal models, and in vitro assays used to establish carcinogenic risk.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by discussing everyday risk-benefit decisions regarding carcinogen exposure and summarizing the main takeaways.
